sentences: Apollo 11 (July 16–24, 1969) was the American mission that first landed humans on the Moon.
Armstrong and Aldrin landed the Eagle in the Sea of Tranquility while Collins orbited in Columbia.
Armstrong walked on the Moon about six hours after landing, with Aldrin following nineteen minutes later.
The crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on July 24 after returning to lunar orbit.
Armstrong's moonwalk was broadcast live to an estimated 600 million viewers.
The Soviet Union could not match the Saturn V, and its probe Luna 15 crashed on the Moon July 21.
The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on October 4, 1957, sparking fears about Soviet capabilities.
Eisenhower responded to Sputnik by creating NASA and initiating Project Mercury.
Kennedy told Congress on May 25, 1961, that the nation should land a man on the Moon before the decade ends.
Kennedy chose a challenge beyond existing rocket capabilities so both countries would start from an equal position.
Kennedy proposed a joint Moon landing to Khrushchev in June 1961, but Khrushchev declined.
In his September 12, 1962 Rice University speech, Kennedy repeated the refrain 'We choose to go to the Moon.'
MIT mathematician Norbert Wiener dubbed the Moon program a 'moondoggle' amid widespread opposition.
NASA head James Webb announced in July 1962 that lunar orbit rendezvous would be used for Apollo.
The lunar module's descent stage landed on the Moon, and its ascent stage returned astronauts to lunar orbit.
The Apollo 1 fire on January 27, 1967 killed three astronauts and abruptly halted the program.
Apollo 7 through 10 tested the spacecraft in Earth and lunar orbit before Apollo 11 was ready.
chunk1: Apollo 11 (July 16–24, 1969) was the American spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon and the fifth crewed Apollo mission.
Commander Neil Armstrong, Command Module Pilot Michael Collins, and Lunar Module Pilot Buzz Aldrin each were on their second and final spaceflight.
The Saturn V launched Apollo 11 from Kennedy Space Center, Florida, on July 16 at 13:32 UTC.
The command module housed the three astronauts and was the only part that returned to Earth; the service module supplied propulsion, power, oxygen, and water.
Armstrong and Aldrin landed the LM Eagle in the Sea of Tranquility on July 20 at 20:17 UTC while Collins remained in lunar orbit aboard Columbia.
